newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Sierra Leone envoy suspects Liberians behind coup.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone envoy suspects Liberians behind coup.

text.p: Sierra Leone's ambassador to the United Nations James Jonah says he suspects Liberians masterminded the coup that toppled President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah a week ago.

"It is suspected that they are Liberian because when they speak on radio they have a Liberian accent," Jonah told Zimbabwe state media late on Saturday when he arrived in the country to represent Kabbah at an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit beginning on Monday.
"People in Sierra Leone are concerned because the people who speak on radio have a different accent from us," he said.

Jonah said he would heavily lobby at the summit for concrete steps to be taken to reverse the coup soon, pointing out the 53-member OAU had condemned coups in the past but done little to back its words.
He cited Burundi where Pierre Buyoya was first isolated by the OAU after staging a coup over a year ago but has since been admitted into the organisation's ranks.
